data.title: Germany's Monday power price jumps on heating demand, below-normal wind
data.description:
The German spot electricity contract for Monday delivery rose on Friday, as cold weather was expected to keep heating demand high and wind output was forecast below the seasonal average.

  • The German baseload spot electricity contract (TRDEBD3) rose 35.0% to €263 ($289) per megawatt hour at 0950 GMT, LSEG data showed

  • The French equivalent contract (TRFRBD3) was untraded

  • German wind power generation is forecast to rise 3.4 GW from Friday to 15.2 GW on Monday, but remains 9.6 GW below the average

  • French wind output is projected to rise 0.1 GW to 3.8 GW, which is 4.6 GW less than the average, the data showed

  • "German wind output stays moderate ... while there are also very weak levels in France," analysts at Engie's EnergyScan said in a note, adding that solar output remained limited by snow and fog

  • Solar power generation in Germany is expected to fall 1.2 GW to 2.1 GW, while French solar output is seen down 0.1 GW at 1.9 GW

  • Consumption in Germany is expected to rise 0.6 GW to 65.9 GW, while French consumption is seen down 0.5 GW at 65.4 GW, LSEG data showed

  • French nuclear availability fell 4 percentage points to 73% of total capacity

  • Along the curve, the French 2027 baseload contract (TRFRBD3) fell 1.6% to €113.9/MWh, LSEG data showed

  • The equivalent German contract (TRDEBYc1) was down 0.9% at €143.25/MWh

  • Mind Energy analysts said they expected the German front-year contract to fall alongside gas prices on Friday

  • European wholesale gas prices fell, driven by milder temperature forecasts and higher Norwegian supply

  • The European carbon market's benchmark contract edged up 0.7% to €84.75 a metric ton

($1 = 0.9107 euros)

data.title: SAP seeks to cut sizeable number of jobs, sources say
data.description:
German business software company SAP is preparing to cut a sizeable number of jobs, two people familiar with the matter told Reuters on Friday.

The works council has not yet been informed about the plans, said one of the sources.

Bloomberg News reported late on Thursday that SAP is considering cutting at least 10,000 jobs in an AI-driven restructuring, citing people familiar with the matter.

CEO Christian Klein and Chief Financial Officer Dominik Asam indicated at investor events in recent weeks that a reduction of the group's workforce of more than 110,000 was on the cards.

In early 2024, the group said it would review 8,000 jobs but cutbacks in slow-growing businesses have since been offset by new hires in more dynamics areas.

Recent moves have pointed to a more cost-conscious approach. An SAP executive told Reuters last month the company was replacing some expensive AI models powering its products with cheaper alternatives.

data.title: Rane eyes new OEMs to cut Maruti dependence as debt, margin pressures persist
data.description:
Chennai-based auto components maker Rane (Madras) (RML) is stepping up efforts to diversify its customer base and reduce its heavy dependence on Maruti Suzuki, even as rising debt, warranty-related provisions and delayed margin recovery continue to weigh on its financial performance.

The company aims to bring three new automakers into its steering business portfolio by FY29 and reduce Maruti Suzuki’s contribution, which currently accounts for about 85 per cent of steering revenues. Chairman Harish Lakshman said two new customers have already been secured and could generate annual revenue of ₹250-260 crore at peak production, while discussions with a third customer are expected to fructify around 2028.

“The low margin continues to bother us,” Lakshman said, underlining the profitability challenges in the steering business despite a healthy order pipeline.

The diversification push comes alongside an aggressive investment programme. RML has raised its FY27 capital expenditure plan to ₹300 crore from the earlier ₹240-250 crore estimate and spent nearly ₹150 crore in the first half, largely on steering, linkage and brake component capacities.

However, growth investments have coincided with mounting leverage. RML’s net debt-to-equity ratio increased to 1.15 times at the end of September from 0.94 times three months earlier, driven by capital expenditure, the acquisition of Hindustan Composites’ friction business and higher working capital requirements.

Management has softened its stance on debt reduction, with Lakshman indicating leverage could remain around current levels for some time. While the company had earlier targeted a net debt-to-equity ratio of 0.5 times by March 2028, it is now unable to provide a clear timeline on when debt levels will decline significantly.

Adding to concerns, Rane Holdings’ 49 per cent-owned safety systems joint venture, ZF Lifetec Rane Automotive India, booked an additional post-tax warranty provision of ₹41.5 crore during the September quarter. The venture’s cumulative warranty provision has risen to €31 million from €23 million disclosed in August, with management expecting clarity on the related recall liability only between July and December 2027.

To support the business and export opportunities, partners have already infused around Rs 165 crore of equity into the venture, with further capital injections remaining a possibility.

While RML secured lifetime orders worth ₹614 crore in the September quarter after a record ₹2,040 crore in the preceding quarter, profitability remains under pressure. EBITDA margin improved marginally by 21 basis points to 9.2 per cent, but management said achieving sustainable double-digit margins could be delayed by another one to two quarters amid persistent cost pressures, supply-chain disruptions and commodity-price volatility.

Despite the operational challenges, Rane reported a sharp rise in consolidated net profit to ₹326.7 crore in the second quarter, aided by a ₹292.1 crore post-tax gain from the sale of land. Revenue rose 34.5 per cent year-on-year to ₹1,242.3 crore. Export-focused growth remained strong, with overseas business contributing 59 per cent of order wins during the quarter.

“Our growth opportunities are promising, but there are multiple challenges in managing costs,” Lakshman said.

data.title: Lemon Tree Hotels opens Keys Select property in Pali, Maharashtra
data.description:
Lemon Tree Hotels Limited has announced the opening of Keys Select by Lemon Tree Hotels, Pali, taking the Group's operational portfolio in Maharashtra to 17 hotels, with another 15 properties in the development pipeline. The property operates under a franchise agreement.

Located in Pali in the Raigad district, the hotel caters to pilgrims, leisure travellers and corporate guests. The town is home to the Shri Ballaleshwar Temple, one of the eight Ashtavinayak shrines, and is surrounded by the Sahyadri ranges. Its proximity to industrial hubs also contributes to corporate travel demand.

The property features 54 rooms and suites across four categories: Business Room, Superior Room, Deluxe Room and Studio Suite. Its food and beverage offerings include Keys Cafe, serving Indian, Continental and regional cuisine, and Unlock Bar. The hotel also features a boardroom for business meetings and a swimming pool.

Commenting on the opening, Vishvapreet Singh Cheema, President, Lemon Tree Hotels Limited, said, “Pali’s unique blend of spiritual heritage, natural beauty, and growing industrial activity makes it an interesting market for organised hospitality. With the opening of Keys Select by Lemon Tree Hotels, Pali, we are delighted to bring Lemon Tree’s signature warmth and dependable comfort to a wider range of travellers. This marks our 17th operational hotel in Maharashtra, with 15 more properties in the pipeline, further strengthening our presence in the state.”

Located on Pali-Khopoli Road, the hotel offers access to attractions including Ballaleshwar Ganpati Temple, approximately 7 km away, Ganesh Gufa, Durshet Forest and Nature Trails, Buddha Vihar, Karnala Bird Sanctuary and Matheran. Navi Mumbai International Airport is approximately 68 km away, while Khopoli Railway Station is 25 km and Pali Bus Station is 7 km from the property.

data.title: Libas Revenue Rises 19% To Rs 726 Cr In FY26; Net Loss Narrows To Rs 15.2 Cr
data.description:
On the cost front, cost of materials consumed remained the largest expense component, rising 34.6 per cent to Rs 426.7 crore in FY26 from Rs 316.9 crore in FY25

India’s ethnic wear market is witnessing intensifying competition from established brands such as Biba, Manyavar and Fabindia, alongside newer labels targeting demand for contemporary ethnic and fusion wear. Brands such as Libas are expanding their omnichannel presence through traditional designs and affordable pricing, as online shopping and organised retail create opportunities beyond metro cities. However, rising sourcing, marketing and distribution costs continue to weigh on the sector.

Against this backdrop, Gurugram-based Libas reported a 19 per cent year-on-year growth in revenue from operations to Rs 726 crore in the financial year ended March 2026. However, the ethnic wear brand remained loss-making, although its net loss narrowed marginally, as per its financial statements filed with the Registrar of Companies (RoC).

Libas FY26 Financial Performance

Founded in 1985, Libas is a women’s fashion brand offering ethnic and fusion wear, including kurtas, suits, sarees, lehengas, dresses and bottom wear. The brand caters to traditional and contemporary fashion preferences through its online platform and offline stores.

Apparel sales remained the company’s sole source of revenue in FY26.

On the cost front, cost of materials consumed remained the largest expense component, rising 34.6 per cent to Rs 426.7 crore in FY26 from Rs 316.9 crore in FY25. It accounted for around 57.4 per cent of the company’s total expenses.

Employee benefit expenses, the second-largest cost component, increased 53 per cent to Rs 67.7 crore from Rs 44.3 crore. Advertising and promotional expenses also rose 17.9 per cent to Rs 66 crore from Rs 56 crore.

Meanwhile, selling and distribution costs declined 20.2 per cent to Rs 46.1 crore. Fabrication expenses, covering garment stitching, processing and finishing, fell 32.5 per cent to Rs 40.35 crore during the year.

Other operating and administrative overheads, including rent, legal and professional fees, transportation and other expenses, also contributed to the company’s overall expenditure.

Consequently, Libas’ total expenses increased 19.6 per cent to Rs 742.8 crore in FY26 from Rs 621.2 crore in FY25.

The company reported a net loss of Rs 15.2 crore, a 7.9 per cent improvement from Rs 16.5 crore in the previous fiscal. However, it remained EBITDA-positive, with an operating surplus of Rs 4 crore during the year.

Margins And Financial Position

Libas’ Return on Capital Employed (ROCE) stood at -9.04 per cent, while its EBITDA margin was 0.55 per cent. On a unit basis, the company spent Rs 1.02 to generate every rupee of operating revenue.

As of March 2026, Libas had total current assets of Rs 377.6 crore, including cash and bank balances of Rs 41.4 crore.

In May 2024, the company raised Rs 150 crore, equivalent to USD 18 million, from IAF Series 5, a fund managed by ICICI Venture, in its maiden external funding round.

Libas Versus Peers

Libas operates in a competitive ethnic wear market that includes established players such as Biba Fashion and Vedant Fashions, the parent company of Manyavar and Mohey.

Biba Fashion reported revenue of around Rs 765 crore in FY25, while Vedant Fashions recorded revenue of Rs 1,436 crore in FY26.

The comparison highlights the scale of competition in India’s organised ethnic wear market, where brands are balancing revenue growth with profitability and rising operating costs.

data.title: Jet Airways Staff To Receive Rs 480 Crore In PF, Gratuity Dues
data.description:
NCLAT directs the airline's liquidator to clear employees' pending statutory benefits with interest within two weeks, ending a seven-year legal battle

Former employees of Jet Airways are set to receive around Rs 480 crore in pending provident fund (PF) and gratuity dues, along with interest, after the National Company Law Appellate Tribunal (NCLAT) directed the airline's liquidator to complete the payments within two weeks.

Under the tribunal's directions, gratuity payments will be transferred directly to eligible employees' bank accounts, while provident fund contributions will be routed through the Employees' Provident Fund (EPF) office into their respective accounts.

The order brings relief to employees who have been pursuing their statutory benefits through a prolonged legal battle since the airline suspended operations in April 2019. A detailed copy of the latest NCLAT order is awaited.

The latest direction follows the appellate tribunal's June 30, 2026 ruling that employees were entitled to their full PF and gratuity dues, irrespective of whether Jet Airways had maintained separate funds for these statutory liabilities. NCLAT had rejected appeals by State Bank of India and other financial creditors, who argued that the employee dues should form part of the airline's liquidation estate.

The Supreme Court subsequently declined to interfere with the appellate tribunal's findings, allowing the employees' entitlement to remain intact.

The dispute gained significance after Jet Airways entered insolvency proceedings and was eventually ordered into liquidation by the Supreme Court in November 2024. The court set aside the resolution plan involving the Jalan-Kalrock Consortium after the consortium failed to fulfil its payment obligations to creditors.

The latest order reinforces the principle that statutory employee benefits such as provident fund and gratuity cannot be treated as ordinary assets available for distribution among creditors during liquidation.

Jet Airways, founded by Naresh Goyal, grounded its operations in April 2019 following financial difficulties. The airline's liquidation brought an end to its proposed revival, leaving former employees waiting for their outstanding employment benefits.

data.title: European shares rise on tech, miners strength; head for weekly gains
data.description:
Key points:
  • Miners jump as copper and gold prices rise
  • ASML, Infineon lead semiconductor stocks rally
  • STOXX 600 set for weekly gains despite tech volatility

By Anjana Jayakrishnan Nair

The European share benchmark rose on Friday, with miners and technology stocks leading gains, as investors prepared to end the week strong despite new US tariff proposals and the prospect of higher interest rates.

The pan-European STOXX 600 joined global stock markets that rose sharply following a US holiday lull that gave some respite from AI jitters.

The benchmark gained 1% to 643.52 points by 0933 GMT, its highest level in a week and its sharpest gain since mid-May. For the week, it was up nearly 3%, bouncing from the steepest weekly decline since late March 2025 posted last week.

"There doesn't seem to be any firm catalyst behind the bounce that we've seen, but it has been a very bruising month. What we're seeing here is dip buyers coming in," said Fiona Cincotta, senior market analyst at StoneX.

European technology stocks (.SX8P) added 2.6% on Friday, led by semiconductor shares ASML , ASM International and Infineon , which gained between 5% and 6%. For the week, the index was 1% higher.

Mining stocks (.SXPP) jumped more than 4% as copper and gold prices rose. Fresnillo and Pan African Resources rose more than 6% each.

Defence stocks rose, with Rheinmetall up 4.2% after a report on a planned AI-platform partnership with Deutsche Telekom.

The broader aerospace and defence index (.SXPARO) gained 2% after Bloomberg News reported the European Union was planning new funds to replace the US war-fighting capabilities.

Investors, meanwhile, shrugged off the Trump administration's move to propose tariffs on goods from the EU.

"The market has a lot of other worries that it's been pricing in. I don't think it is seeing tariffs as a major headwind," Cincotta said.

Consumer-facing foods and beverages (.SX3P) and personal and household goods (.SXQP) were among the weakest performers, with sportswear makers Adidas and Puma down around 1.4% and 1.3%, respectively.

Data this week showed US inflation rose further last month, and the economy grew more than previously expected, adding to bets on interest rate hikes.

Markets await Sunday's snap election in Spain, called by Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez after parliament rejected housing measures aimed at tackling a crisis that has triggered protests across the country.

Among other individual stocks, Thales gained 2% after French laser technology company Lumibird said it had entered exclusive talks to sell a controlling stake to the defence group. Lumibird surged 18.5%.

data.title: The AI stock crash is mostly over, JPMorgan says - but a worse phase could be coming in 2027
data.description:
By Steve Goldstein

'Three phases of the bear' framework points to a rebound, but then a drift lower

JPMorgan's European quants expect a rebound followed by a drift lower.

The crash in artificial-intelligence stocks has just about run its course, but a worse phase could be in store for next year.

That's the conclusion of a team led by Khuram Chaudhry, head of European quantitative strategy at JPMorgan. Though the research was focused on European equities, it has obvious parallels with the action in the larger U.S. stock market.

They point to a "three phrases of the bear" framework, which are crash, rebound and drift lower. That was the case of the drawdowns during the dot-com bubble, the global financial crisis, the pandemic and then the 2022 rates shock/Russian invasion.

"Historically, this process lasts on average about 18 months, and we feel the recent momentum sell-off is likely a re-emergence of this first stage (crash), and a shift to the second stage (rebound) may soon follow," they say.

That looked to be the case on Friday, with U.S. stock-market futures (ES00) (NQ00) rallying and the Stoxx Europe 600 XX:SXXP up over 1%.

Looking at the current situation, the strategists say the bank's own measure of global investor sentiment has only been this depressed on five prior occasions in the last 20 years, each during a major growth shock.

They noted that fundamentals - either in the form of analyst earnings estimates or in the purchasing managers indexes - do not support such a downturn. That supports a rebound.

But this rebound may then be met with a drift lower. "We believe a regime change is underway, with an economic growth slowdown being the main risk to global markets in 2027, particularly if central banks run the risk of tightening into a slowing growth phase," they say.

During such a regime change, macro indicators will be volatile, and during peaks and troughs in the cycle data is notoriously mixed and fickle, they say.

They say JPMorgan's U.S. quant macro index is in expansion territory, but near levels where mean reversion is expected. The ratio of orders to inventories in the U.S. Institute for Supply Management manufacturing index has already peaked, even though the headline index remains healthy.

"For now, the fragility of growth is not a consensus view, with markets pricing in more than two rate hikes through the first quarter. In our view, tighter policy adds to the threat of a deeper slowdown, and may be a policy mistake. If activity slows more than expected, further downside - and a drift to new lows - cannot be ruled out," they say.

-Steve Goldstein

data.title: Eni bets on Latin American growth with Argentina LNG project approval imminent
data.description:
Key points:
  • Eni broadens growth beyond Africa and Europe
  • Investment decision on Argentina LNG expected Monday, sources say
  • Eni says gross output at Venezuelan Junin 5 field could reach 1 million boed by 2033
  • Gross output from Eni's Latam projects could grow to around 1.4 million boed by 2033, Reuters calculations show

By Francesca Landini and Shadia Nasralla

Eni and its partners are expected to take a final investment decision on their $51 billion Argentina LNG project on Monday, two people with direct knowledge of the matter said, as the Italian energy group accelerates growth in Latin America to diversify beyond its traditional focus on Africa and Europe.

Eni is seeking to secure alternative sources of energy for Europe through stakes in projects in Argentina and Venezuela with a total gross production of at least 1.4 million boed of oil and gas over the next seven years, according to Reuters calculations based on official documents.

The Italian group is looking across the Atlantic as sanctions and conflicts have curtailed energy flows from Russia and the Middle East.

Developed with Argentina's state-controlled YPF and UAE energy investment company XRG, the Argentina LNG project aims to monetise gas from the Vaca Muerta shale formation and help turn Argentina into a global exporter of LNG.

The first phase is expected to produce 12 million metric tons per year of LNG through two floating LNG units scheduled to start production by 2030. Eni's share of the output would amount to about 84,000 boed, based on a 32% stake in the project, according to Reuters calculations.

A third LNG vessel could eventually lift capacity to as much as 18 mtpa, according to YPF and Eni.

The project was included in Argentina's RIGI investment incentive programme, the country's energy minister said last week, while YPF has said a final investment decision could come as early as November.

VENEZUELA GROWTH

In Venezuela, Eni owns a 50% stake in the 100,000 boed Perla gas field alongside Spain's Repsol . Together with interests in other producing assets such as Corocoro, Eni's Venezuelan production averaged about 64,000 boed last year.

Eni is, however, expanding its presence in the country. In September it became the sole operator of the Junin 5 heavy oil field, one of Venezuela's largest undeveloped fields.

Junin 5 could reach 200,000 boed within 18 to 24 months of a final investment decision, which Eni expects by the end of 2026, Chief Operating Officer for Natural Resources Guido Brusco said during a third-quarter results call.

Gross output from the field could eventually rise to 1 million boed by 2032-2033, Brusco said. Eni has yet to disclose its stake in Junin 5 under the new contract signed in September.

Eni's total global oil and gas production was around 1.7 million boed last year, with Latin America accounting for roughly 7% of the total, including Mexico.

data.title: Palm oil posts over 2% weekly gains on rival oils at Dalian
data.description:
By Dewi Kurniawati

Malaysian palm oil futures rose on Friday, supported by gains in rival vegetable oils at the Dalian market and a technical rebound from recent lows, with the benchmark posting a 2.13% weekly gain.

The benchmark palm oil contract for February delivery on the Bursa Malaysia Derivatives Exchange added 15 ringgit, or 0.35%, to 4,307 ringgit ($1,046.15) a metric ton at the close.

"The futures' increase is mainly driven by technical rebound after the recent double bottom while tracking Dalian performance," a Kuala Lumpur-based trader said.

Palm oil tracks the price movements of rival edible oils as it competes for a share of the global vegetable oils market.

Dalian's most-active soyoil contract (DBYcv1) rose 1.26%, while its palm oil contract added 2.08%. The Chicago Board of Trade (BOCv1) is on a modified Thanksgiving holiday schedule, with an early close on Friday.

State export monitoring firm Danantara Sumberdaya Indonesia (DSI) is still evaluating the final fee it will charge for its services, the company's chief executive said on Friday.

Palm oil group GAPKI said on Thursday DSI has proposed a service fee of 0.5% of the value of palm oil exports.

Crude palm oil prices are expected to stay above 4,100 ringgit per metric ton in December, as supply risks emerge heading into 2027, the Malaysian Palm Oil Council said on Wednesday.

Exports of Malaysian palm oil products for November 1 to 25 fell 9.3% from October 1 to 25, independent inspection company AmSpec Agri Malaysiasaid, while cargo surveyor Intertek Testing Services estimated a 4% drop.

The ringgit MYR=, palm's currency of trade, weakened 0.13% against the dollar, making the commodity slightly cheaper for buyers holding foreign currencies.

($1 = 4.1170 ringgit)
